<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">
Repo: /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp. One file: cave/runner.js. Implement issue #6 — driver-aware idle-guard toggle.

CONTEXT: runner.js has an in-process idle-guard: bot with no running task for ~60s gets an auto default task (auto-deposit to depot etc., grep "idle-guard" / "idle_guard" / "idleGuard" to find the loop and the 60s threshold). Problem: LLM driver think-gaps >60s are normal, so the guard interleaves with an ACTIVE driver (two-commanders problem). Doctrine: one commander per bot.

IMPLEMENT:
1. New endpoint POST /idleguard, body {"on": true|false}. Sets a runtime flag. Response: {"ok":true,"idleGuard":true|false,"note":...}. Validate body (400 on missing/non-boolean "on").
2. When flag off: idle-guard loop skips firing (log a quiet line at most once per few minutes, not every tick).
3. SAFETY TTL: when off, ANY period of 15+ minutes with ZERO incoming HTTP requests (any endpoint) auto-re-arms the guard (flag back on + one log line + one /events ring entry type "idle-guard" msg "re-armed after 15min driver silence"). Track a lastHttpRequestAt timestamp in the request handling path — cheap, one assignment per request. An abandoned bot must never sit unguarded forever.
4. GET /status response: add field "idleGuard": true|false so drivers see the state.
5. /events ring entry when toggled (type "idle-guard", msg "disabled by driver" / "enabled by driver").

Style: match existing endpoint registration + response patterns in runner.js exactly (look at how /stop or /autoeat are wired). Keep the change tight — no refactors.

VERIFY: node --check cave/runner.js. Report: what you found (where guard loop + threshold live, file:line), what you added (file:line), syntax result. Caveman style, exact refs.
</teammate-message>
